confirm.text: Selection carried forward across forms: Kirschke's two forms carry identical nine-item observation lists on two different jobs the same day. Flores's two forms likewise carry identical eight-item lists. This is the pattern Kelby Hammer described as a training issue rather than a reporting problem.

Paired technicians diverging on the same job: on both 35721 and 35722, Kirschke selected "Stop work authority was discussed" and 1099 Rolando Flores, working the same well in the same hour, selected neither stop-work item. Worth a word with both about what the item means, not a finding against either.
Neither stop-work item selected: Flores on 35721_2 and 35722_2; 1099 Joseph Popillion on BRUNSON 35 6 (35405, a 10/10 job).

One form is not the mis-selection pattern. Jerry Gonzales on XTO UNIVERSITY 2-20 56H (35714_2) selected both "Unsafe conditions" and "Stop work authority was discussed". This is a 10/10/2026 job whose form arrived on 10/11, so it belongs to Friday's count, not Sunday's. The form contains no narrative naming an unsafe condition — "What Did We Observe? Continued" reads only "Crew we connect to well after having meeting" — so there is nothing on the record that either supports or rules out a real condition. It needs Gonzales's confirmation. Note also that the same form's Location Sign and both Exxon JSA uploads returned "Image not available:Picture capture file empty" with a 10/09/2026 timestamp, so the supporting documentation for that job is effectively absent.
No technician on this list appeared on the stop-work confirmation lists reported for 09/23 or 09/26.

No job board was available for 10/11/2026, so the coverage check could not be run as normal. Blake Walton's most recent board email is 10/8/2026; there is none for 10/9, 10/10 or 10/11. The October Permian workbook on that email contains sheets only through "10-9 DRAFT", and the 10-9 sheet is a Friday draft that does not list any of Sunday's XTO AGT jobs or their assigned technicians. Using it to assert Sunday assignments would be wrong, so no gap below is stated as confirmed. Nothing here should be actioned until a board for 10/11 is available.
What can be checked without a board is whether each trailer that appeared in the day's forms received its two Trailer Inspection Forms and one Trailer Readiness Form:

Trailer 601 — requirement met. Three Trailer Inspection Forms (Stefanie Kirschke 06:28 AM at the Andrews shop; 1099 Rolando Flores 12:37 PM at Lenorah; Kirschke 02:17 PM at Midland) and one Trailer Readiness Form (Flores 03:31 PM). More than required, not fewer.

Trailer 607 — requirement met, all three by one technician. Dawson Drake filed both Trailer Inspection Forms (07:57 AM at the Andrews shop, 10:15 AM at W County Rd 320, Midkiff) and the Trailer Readiness Form (11:48 AM). This is allowed — the requirement counts across the crew, so one technician filing all three is not a finding and should not be chased.

Trailer 602 — one Trailer Inspection Form received (Andrew Bailey, 11:10 AM, Andrews shop); second Trailer Inspection Form not received; Trailer Readiness Form not received. Note the tire defect above: if 602 was pulled from service and never deployed, no further forms would be expected. Needs the board and a word with the shop before it is treated as a gap.

Trailer 503 — one Trailer Inspection Form received (Andrew Bailey, 11:30 AM, Andrews shop); second Trailer Inspection Form not received; Trailer Readiness Form not received. Whether 503 was assigned to a job on Sunday cannot be established without the board.

Air jobs. Every air job that produced a form on 10/11 has one submission per named technician, which is the requirement: RHAEGAL UNIT 4664DH (Kirschke 35721_1, Flores 35721_2), Crawford Welchest 27K #11H (Kirschke 35722_1, Flores 35722_2), TXL 27 UNIT 3 2773JH (Drake 35678, Fontenot 35679). All six jobs were ENDED, none paused. Whether any further air jobs were assigned and produced nothing cannot be checked without the board.
Confined space. No confined space jobs appear in the day's submissions.

Supervision. Four H2S Safety Supervision Daily Inspection Forms were received, from Dennis Easley (Comstock, kern), Bobby Fleming (SM Energy, Blue Marlin Fed Com 212H), Larry Taylor (Comstock, Patterson 904) and 1099 Hayden Haugh (Ovintiv, H&P 616). Shift coverage — whether each assigned day and night tech filed for their own shift — cannot be checked without the board, and that check normally turns up 1099 contractor absences. As noted previously, it is still not established whether every 1099 contractor is set up to file in StreetSmart, so a form that was never expected is not a form that is missing.
Field service. No field service jobs appear in the day's submissions, so the trailer-delivery inspection check does not arise.

One multi-day supervision close-out needs a look on its own merits. Justin Pack closed ETX Mitsui E&P Flowback Lipsey 1H (35241_1) at 05:34 PM on 10/11 after a run that began 10/01. The daily start entries stop at 10/08; the 10/08 pause carries a duration of 3d:0h:0m and there are no daily starts for 10/09, 10/10 or 10/11. The close-out reads "Details if Any: I gave ticket to Marcos to give to bray I left on Thursday" and was submitted from Leesburg, TX — roughly 100 miles from the Oakwood worksite used on every prior day. This is a timekeeping and hand-off question for the ETX side rather than a safety finding.

doc.text: Bottle Hydro Dates and cascade pressures

Both fields carry values on both forms; neither is a finding. Fleming's hydro string is run together without separators and is hard to read back — worth asking him to space the entries, but the data is there.

Larry Taylor — both "Pressure on Cascade System" and "Bottle Hydro Dates" were submitted blank. All six air-trailer photo fields and the Condition Sign & Flags photo on the same form are also empty, which is what the form looks like when there is no air trailer on location. If the board shows AT# = N/A for Patterson 904, these are expected to be empty and this is not a finding. Needs the board to resolve; do not raise it with Taylor until it is.

1099 Hayden Haugh — both fields entered as "N/a", with the same six air-trailer photo fields empty. Same situation as Taylor: consistent with no trailer on location at Ovintiv H&P 616, needs AT# confirmation.

All four charged bottles carry both a pressure and a hydro date — complete, not a finding. The 02/23 hydro date on bottle 2 is the oldest on the trailer and may be worth a look on its own.

Larry Taylor — H2S daily at Comstock Patterson 904: every photo captured on the day, all four compliance questions answered Yes, comments N/A, subject only to the AT# confirmation noted above. Dawson Drake — the 10:15 AM Trailer Inspection Form for trailer 607 at Midkiff, all photos same-day. Andrew Bailey — Trailer Inspection Form for trailer 503, all eleven photos same-day.

Trailer forms of both kinds and the equipment sections of the H2S daily are photo-based, so a defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside images, not as text, so they cannot be read or checked here. A second limitation applies today: this review ran at 11:00 PM Central on the day being reviewed, so submissions that land overnight or tomorrow morning for Sunday's work have not been captured and the usual next-morning sweep for late arrivals could not be run.

23 of 23 submissions read. The job board was NOT available for 10/11/2026 — Blake Walton's most recent board email is 10/8/2026 and its Permian workbook contains sheets only through "10-9 DRAFT", so no sheet for the day reviewed exists. 0 manned board rows were checked for coverage, and the coverage section above rests on the forms alone.
